title: Ghost-hunter terrorised by blood-chilling spook
excerpt: A paranormal investigator has revealed the most frightening moment of his ghost-hunting career.
content:
A paranormal investigator has revealed the most frightening moment of his ghost-hunting career.

A ghost-hunter has revealed his spookiest moment

Colin Browen - who hosts the Murder In America podcast and The Paranormal Files on YouTube - has spent 11 years looking into potential hauntings and he's now recalled the terrifying moment he ran out of a former asylum building after seeing a woman's hand appear in front of him.

During an appearance on ARC Maine, he said: "I've seen so much over the last 11 years. I have stories for days. Seen things levitate in front of me, thrown at us, doors slamming, seeing full bodied figures, shadow figures.

"This one time was very creepy in this asylum I saw what looked like a woman's hand. I looked with my flashlight to the left and there's this pillar and we're in the basement of this old asylum and when I looked at the pillar there was just this hand on the side of the pillar.

"And I just watched with my eyes as it went [withdrew] and disappeared behind the pillar. So needless to say after that, we got out of there fast."

Colin has previously admitted that not all hauntings are scary and there are plenty of "happy, jovial spirits" who just want to have a bit of a "laugh".

He told the US Mirror: "I've investigated dozens of homes and places that were filled with happy, jovial spirits - in fact, one night, we spent the entire night telling jokes to the spirits and watched as they played with our devices and seemingly laughed along with us."

Colin blames Hollywood horror movies and documentaries for the negative perception of hauntings, adding: "In horror movies and documentaries about the paranormal world, usually hauntings are portrayed as intense, frightening and disturbing; however, in real life, it's never black and white.

"Although it's possible you may run into something more on the negative side, and you may not be dealing with Casper, most of the time, the spirits we encounter and interact with seem to be lost souls, in a way - not angry, demonic beings intent on raising hell - simply energies and spiritual entities that we don't really understand."

Colin went on to insist most ghosts aren't interested in hurting humans and often they just want acknowledgement or help. He added: "[Often they want] be acknowledged ... [or] helped with a task or given some form of respect."
